title: Does the qualified expert need feedback, or only a replayed gait?
hypothesis: The PPO expert maintains sustained axial roll through state-dependent corrections that a clock-only replay of its successful actions cannot reproduce across reset placements.

prediction.against: clock-only replay of one frozen successful PPO demonstration
prediction.rationale: On Stage 3, a gain of at least 0.20 with a paired t interval above zero would justify teaching trace repair feedback relationships rather than an action sequence.

protocol.command: gpu run 'bash -lc "source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study feedback_ablation"'
code_changes: scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py: add the declared study selector and a clock-only action-tape controller; reuse the manifest-driven evaluator.
config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml: freeze two 40-case manifests, Stage 3, and the qualified D-036 seed-4020 model_8239 checkpoint by resolved path and hash.
Select the first sustained-success demonstration by manifest order, not evaluation performance; replay its complete 360-action sequence without observation feedback or retiming.

Run demonstration collection once, closed-loop PPO twice, and replay once, each in a separate Isaac process at batch size 40. Abort if PPO repeats have any outcome flips or more than 4/40 diverged environments.
Record the unchanged D-034 sustained reducer, tail-hit fraction, axial/transverse angular velocity, and action traces; do not promote or change the reducer.

falsified_by: The paired interval's upper bound is below +0.20; an interval spanning zero is inconclusive, and tied success is not an improvement.

direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: Run this first: 160 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls provide a cheap comparison of the qualified expert against a frozen action tape, with separate-process reproducibility checks and the sustained reducer unchanged. Its main limitation is inferential: failure of this tape would not establish that every clock-only controller needs feedback. Retain the prediction of paired_success_difference increasing by at least 0.20 against the frozen replay and its upper-bound-below-0.20 falsifier; intervals including zero remain inconclusive.

implementer.reasoning: Agree: cheap (160 episodes, 0 calls), one process per cell, unchanged D-034 reducer, and it answers a question trace repair depends on: whether the expert's traces carry feedback relationships or only a tape. Will add the tape controller to the existing evaluator rather than a new rollout loop, and abort on a failed reproducibility gate.
